title: Towards more accurate natural orbital functional approximations: including 4-index cumulant contributions
authors: Valerii Chuiko, Paul W. Ayers, Eduard Matito
abstract: Accurate modeling of bond breaking remains a central challenge for reduced density matrix functional theory (RDMFT). Although some modern functionals can yield reasonably accurate dissociation energies, they often fail to reproduce key properties of the dissociated fragments, such as a vanishing fragment population covariance (also known as the delocalization index) and the correct total spin angular momentum of each fragment (local spin). In this work, we revisit the construction of natural orbital functionals by correcting the cumulant contribution produced by the PNOF5 functional. Our method enforces known contributions of the cumulant to local spin fragments and the delocalization index at the dissociation limit. We obtain the closest cumulant consistent with these physically motivated constraints and subsequently purify the corresponding one- and two-electron reduced density matrices by imposing the standard $P, Q, \text{and } G$ $N$-representability conditions. The resulting functional yields improved behavior in strongly correlated regimes. Benchmarking on the dissociation of the singlet states of \ce{N2}, \ce{NO+}, \ce{O2}, \ce{S2}, and \ce{CO} shows that in the dissociation regime the energies computed from the updated cumulant exactly reproduce the complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) energies. We further analyze the limitations of the approach and identify scenarios in which the current approach performs poorly. This work provides a pathway for systematically improving natural orbital functionals to achieve reliable bond-breaking calculations within RDMFT.
summary: This paper improves Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory (RDMFT) by systematically correcting natural orbital functionals using 4-index cumulant contributions. The method enforces strict physical constraints derived from the asymptotic behavior of fragment spin and delocalization indices upon bond breaking. This leads to highly accurate energy predictions that match high-level CASSCF calculations in the dissociation limit.
main_problem: Developing more accurate natural orbital functional approximations for Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory (RDMFT) to correctly model bond breaking.
main_result: The updated functional, incorporating 4-index cumulant contributions and enforcing physical constraints, reproduces CASSCF energies exactly in the dissociation regime for benchmark molecules like N2 and O2.
method: The authors correct the PNOF5 functional by minimizing the distance to a target cumulant while imposing linear constraints derived from known asymptotic behaviors of local spin and delocalization indices.
model_or_system: The study focuses on electronic structure calculations using RDMFT, specifically analyzing the dissociation process of diatomic molecules (e.g., N2, O2) into two fragments.
key_observables: Bond dissociation energies, fragment population covariance (delocalization index), local spin angular momentum ($\langle \hat{S}^2 angle$), and cumulant elements ($\Gamma_{ij;kl}$).
important_parameters: The dissociation limit ($|R_{AB}|	o\infty$) is the critical regime analyzed for benchmarking.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that enforcing physical constraints on the cumulants can systematically improve functional accuracy, although limitations exist when active electrons are small or far from dissociation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the iterative procedure flowchart and show how constraint violations (P, Q, G conditions) decrease towards convergence during molecular dissociation for various species.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by identifying the failure of existing functionals at bond breaking, proposing a constrained optimization method to correct cumulant contributions, demonstrating convergence through iterative projection onto N-representability, and finally benchmarking against CASSCF results across several molecules.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental limitations in describing static correlation and bond dissociation within quantum chemistry methods, which is crucial for understanding molecular electronic structure dynamics relevant to AMO physics.
